title: Ultrasound & Infrasound
description: Bats, ships and doctors all use sounds you can't hear. Harness ultrasound to reveal fragment 7.

content.value: Many animals hear sounds we cannot. Dogs hear higher frequencies than us (that's how a 'silent' dog whistle works). Bats and dolphins use ULTRASOUND to navigate and hunt, sending out high squeaks and listening for the echoes.

🦇  Bats & dolphins → make & hear ULTRASOUND (echolocation)
🐕  Dogs           → hear higher frequencies than humans
🐘  Elephants/whales → use INFRASOUND to communicate far away

A bat sends out ultrasound and listens for the echo bouncing back off objects and insects. From the echo it works out where things are — even in total darkness. This is called ECHOLOCATION, and ships use a similar idea (SONAR) to measure the depth of the sea.

Humans put ultrasound to work: doctors use ultrasound scans to see inside the body (including checking on unborn babies) safely, without harmful rays. Ultrasound is also used to clean delicate machine parts and jewellery.
Ultrasound is safe and useful precisely because it's just high-frequency sound — the same physics as a whistle, only pitched too high for our ears.

Key Takeaway: Ultrasound (above 20,000 Hz) is used by bats and dolphins for echolocation and by humans for medical scans and cleaning. Infrasound (below 20 Hz) is used by animals like elephants to communicate over long distances.

quiz.question: Bats find their way in the dark using…
quiz.explain: Bats emit ultrasound and listen to the echoes to locate objects — echolocation.

quiz.question: One helpful human use of ultrasound is…
quiz.explain: Doctors use ultrasound scans to see inside the body safely.

quiz.question: A 'silent' dog whistle works because dogs can hear…
quiz.explain: Dogs hear higher frequencies than we do, so the whistle sounds silent to us but not to them.
